settings.description: Canal & Quire is an independent bookshop and reading club. Start at the staff shelf or bring one good question to the next discussion.

settings.title: From the staff shelf
settings.description: Three books for different kinds of afternoons.

items.title: A river of voices
items.description: The Living Mountain by Nan Shepherd. Slowly observed walks make room for rock, weather and the ordinary work of paying attention.

items.title: Lives between cities
items.description: The Namesake by Jhumpa Lahiri. A family makes a home across languages, rituals and the distance between generations.

items.title: A short, strange trip
items.description: Invisible Cities by Italo Calvino. Enter anywhere and read one city at a time for an evening of imagined places.

settings.title: Read together
settings.subtitle: READING CLUB
settings.description: A conversation works best when everyone can point to a page.

settings.panel_description: For a first discussion, try The Living Mountain. What does Shepherd notice when getting to the summit stops being the point?

items.title: Read at your own pace
items.description: Come with the whole book, a chapter or a passage you stayed with.

items.title: Bring a question
items.description: A description that surprised you or a sentence you disagreed with is enough to open the conversation.

items.title: Leave with a note
items.description: Write down one detail you heard from someone else and look for it in your next book.

settings.editor: Begin with what happens on the page. Read one short passage aloud and pick a detail everyone can hear.
Move to what it suggests. Ask what each person noticed first and how the choice of words shaped their reading.
End with what stays open. Keep one unanswered question for a second reading or your next meeting.

tabs.tab_title: Can I use an e-book or audiobook?
tabs.tab_content: Yes. Name the chapter and a recognizable line so the group can find the same passage.

tabs.tab_title: What if I have only read a few pages?
tabs.tab_content: Bring one observation from what you did read. Tell the group where you stopped before the discussion starts.

tabs.tab_title: How do we pick the next book?
tabs.tab_content: Bring a title and a short description of why it would lead to a good conversation. Choose something the group can find and read before meeting again.
